newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Japanese businessman and three Filipinos are rescued by a police military task force near Cotabato city, a day after they are kidnapped by suspected Moro Islamic Liberation Front (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Two opposition senators accuse Malacanang and the Commission on Elections of conspiring to make the general voters' registration a failure so as to improve the chances of administration's presidential candidate in 1998 (MANILA TIMES)
- HIV positive woman gives birth to a 5.9 pound healthy baby boy (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos arrives in London to meet officials of the new Labour government and get insight into its foreign policy (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co says an audit of its financial health indicates some of its officers might have been involved in a loan anomaly involving the firms' subsidiary. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Shell Philippines Exploration BV and Occidental Philippines Inc are expected to sign up their first customer, First Gas Holdings Corp, this week. (MANILA TIMES)
- The government posts a 4.92 billion peso budget surplus in the first five months of the year. (BUSINESSWORLD)
